service.description: The services of the artifact index by name, with their component, file, SECA count and the calls of the last spec run.

A service as its view shows it: its definition with the parameters nested (those auto-parameters imply marked), its file and line, its script's file, its SECA rules, what uses it, the last spec run's calls. With files, the definition is the unsaved buffers' (read only, nothing runs).

parameter.name: files
parameter.description: A JSON list of {rootId, path, text}: unsaved service buffers.

service.description: Run a service in the sim, nothing kept: its out-parameters, messages and the rows it would write; or with real and confirm, for real (the extend tier), audited. In the sim it runs as unsaved or proposed text defines it (F14): the service files and script files of files and preview stand at their locations for the Try's own calls only. With trace, each XML actions element's count, the values it set and the one that failed.

parameter.name: files
parameter.description: A JSON list of {rootId, path, text}: unsaved buffers to run over, in the sim only.

parameter.name: preview
parameter.description: buffer:<id> (a canvas or guided editor's buffer) or approval:<id> (a change set of yours) to run over, in the sim only.

service.description: A scratch inline service of XML Actions or JavaScript run in the sim, its messages and rows.
A feature from a Try (call, then, checkData of its rows) appended to the service's spec file, in its component when the user may write there, else in the site's.
A spec file run in process inside the sim, nothing kept: each feature's outcome and each service's calls.
The JavaScript the framework runs for an actions block, each statement after its element.
The active SECA, EECA, EmECA and gitECA rules with their files, priorities, conditions and actions, the rules a later one replaced under it.
A rule's condition (an expression or a condition element) against a context (a JSON object: the service's last Try, a record), run in the sim: whether it holds, with its messages and log.

parameter.name: against
parameter.description: A JSON object: the context the condition reads.

service.description: A context a rule's condition is tried against, saved as a named fixture of the rules file (test/fixtures/<name>.json of its component, or the site's): one of the name is replaced. The extend tier.

parameter.name: path
parameter.description: The rules file.

parameter.name: context
parameter.description: A JSON object.

service.description: The fixtures of a rules file, each with its context.

Save as spec on a rule (10): its fixture written, and a feature appended to the rules file's spec that runs the rule's trigger with it (a SECA's service call, an EECA's entity operation) and checks what the trigger did in a run in the sim now; for a gitECA rule, whose push a spec does not replay, its condition against the fixture. A trigger that fails in the sim writes nothing. The extend tier.

parameter.name: path
parameter.description: The rules file, saved.

parameter.name: kind
parameter.description: seca, eeca or giteca

parameter.name: target
parameter.description: The rule's service (seca) or entity (eeca).

parameter.name: operation
parameter.description: An EECA rule's: create, update or delete.

parameter.name: condition
parameter.description: A gitECA rule's: an expression or a condition element.

parameter.name: fixture
parameter.description: The fixture's name.

parameter.name: context
parameter.description: The fixture: a JSON object.

parameter.name: trial
parameter.description: The trigger's run in the sim.

service.description: A gitECA rule's condition against a push of the push log (10): the hosted repositories the user sees that the rule's repository-pattern takes, the latest changes of the one chosen, and with an update the contexts the rule's event had from it (org.moqui.git.GitServices.get#GitUpdateEventContexts, for who may push there, only the commits the user reads), each marked whether the rule runs on it (its source, ref-pattern, ref-type and default-branch-only, as the rule decides). Run as the user.

parameter.name: refType
parameter.description: branch, tag or other

parameter.name: source
parameter.description: The rule's sources, comma separated; empty is push, fetch and import

parameter.name: event
parameter.description: The rule's event; post-receive when empty.

parameter.name: updates
parameter.description: find#GitUpdates' updateList

parameter.name: contexts
parameter.description: {label, context, matches}

parameter.name: truncated
parameter.description: The replay left contexts or commits out
